To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical coupling of the antiferromagentic Mott transition in graphene is largely insensitive to a realistic static screening and hence that suspended graphene remains a semimetal at realistic interaction strengths.
the critical coupling of the Mott transition is not affected by the long range Coulomb tails.
the long-range Coulomb interaction tails do not affect the Mott transition in graphene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of the Coulomb interaction and the Dirac-like dispersion of the electronic states of graphene.
the electronic properties of the tight-binding Hamiltonian of graphene with partially-screened Coulomb interactions.
the electronic properties of the graphene sheet in the presence of Coulomb interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antiferromagnetism is a rather weak effect, which can be neglected in many cases, and that the semimetal is the ground state of graphene.
the semimetallic phase is stabilized in suspended graphene, while the insulating phase is expected for doped graphene.
the Mott transition in graphene can be realized only in the presence of long-range Coulomb interaction and the absence of any screening.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the long-range Coulomb tail of the screened Coulomb interactions does not change the qualitative behavior of the system, but only the quantitative value of the critical coupling.
the long-range part of the screened Coulomb interactions in suspended graphene is not strong enough to drive an antiferromagnetism at low temperatures.
the Mott transition is robust against the inclusion of realistic static screening effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antiferromagnetism in graphene is a genuine Mott phenomenon and that the screening of the Coulomn interactions is not sufficient to stabilize a magnetic order.
the long-range Coulomb tail is not sufficient to induce a transition to an antiferomagnetic insulating state.
, in contrast to previous studies, the long-range Coulomb interaction does not play a crucial role for the Mott transition in graphene.
